stops.name: Popayán, the last calm crossing
stops.campa: He passes through Popayán at the end of May, resting briefly among acquaintances who will later testify to how plainly he traveled: a small party, little baggage, nothing of the pomp his rank could have claimed. From here the road climbs into the mountains toward Pasto, through the district Obando governs and the pass called Berruecos, a place already ill-famed in the province for ambush. Sucre rides on into it anyway, thirteen leagues short of Pasto.

stops.name: Berruecos, the forest road, four shots, thirty-five years old
stops.campa: On the mountain trail between El Cabuyal and La Jacoba, in the forest called Berruecos, gunmen hired by Colonel Apolinar Morillo and José Erazo, the plot laid, the record shows, at Obando's own instance, fire on Sucre from the trees. Four balls strike him: head, neck, breast. He falls from his mule and dies on the forest path, thirty-five years old, four months and six days before the man he served will die of his own broken health at Santa Marta, calling the murder of Sucre the day something in him could not survive.
stops.quote: ¡Santo Dios! ¡Se ha derramado la sangre de Abel! ... La bala cruel que le hirió el corazón, mató a Colombia y me quitó la vida.
stops.quote_source: Bolívar, on hearing of Sucre's assassination, Cartagena, 1 July 1830 (accounts of his aides; O'Leary, Memorias)
